thread:
marco: Quick follow-up from the split-runner RFC — I pushed a short sketch for a lean handshake between the bench runner and the validator. Need input on three things: retry/backoff semantics, how golden-sample rotation is triggered, and minimal telemetry we need to keep to debug silent failures.

marco: sketch here -> https://go.internal/rfc/split-runner-handshake (short doc, tl;dr below)

priya: skimmed. main worry is the retry window when the validator is overloaded — we should avoid head-of-line blocking on warmup runs.

tess: +1. If bench-runner retries aggressively it will exacerbate backpressure. We should prefer an exponential jittered backoff and then demote to 'deferred' state where the work is enqueued for async recheck.

jordan: can we push that to a simple state machine? e.g., PENDING -> RETRYING (n attempts) -> DEFERRED -> FAIL. That keeps the runner code readable.

marco: yep that's basically the plan. Proposed config (pseudo):

```yaml
handshake:
  attempts: 3
  base_backoff_ms: 200
  max_backoff_ms: 5000
  deferred_ttl_mins: 60
  demote_after: 2  # after 2 rapid fails go to DEFERRED
```

sam: what about golden-sample rotation? we don't want continuous churn that invalidates regressions. My vote: rotation only on approved model promotion or explicit ops request. auto-rotation on drift is risky.

priya: agreed for automatic rotation. But we do need a safety valve: if golden becomes corrupted or missing, we should fall back to a minimal canonical set to unblock smoke runs.

marco: proposal: two-tier golden policy — controlled rotation (manual/promote) + emergency fallback set. Rotation frequency is a manual step in the rollout pipeline.

tess: that respects reproducibility. Also, add a flag in the handshake payload so validator can signal 'golden-mismatch' vs 'golden-missing' vs 'ok'. Runner can then route to ops or use fallback.

bench-bot: note: we've observed ~0.6% silent failures on long-seq model runs when golden hash mismatches but samples still pass. Having a distinct 'mismatch-but-pass' signal will help QA triage.

jordan: telemetry — minimal surface: request_id, model_version, runner_node_id, validator_node_id, handshake_state, latency_ms, failure_reason_code, golden_hash. Keep traces sampled (1%) and full logs for CANARY or ADMIT runs.

priya: add kv-cache-size and seqlen distribution tags — those are often the root cause for hardware-specific regressions.

marco: good call. I can add those fields to the handshake telemetry. Also thinking: make the handshake payload compact JSON and versioned (v1, v2) so we can evolve without breaking older runners.

sam: deployment tradeoff: a single binary that contains both bench-runner and validator libraries is easiest for on-prem but forces co-deploy. The split-runner approach is better for Dedicated/hosted where we can scale validator independently.

tess: ops ask — provide a simple CLI to force a golden-swap and to re-enqueue deferred checks. That avoids building a one-off script each time.

marco: action items:
- i) I'll update the sketch with the state machine + config examples (by EOD).
- ii) @tess to draft the handshake payload fields and telemetry list (today).
- iii) @priya to write a short runbook for fallback golden set usage (tomorrow).
- iv) @jordan to prototype the CLI for swap/requeue (next week).

sam: tiny nit — consider a per-model soft-rate-limit for retries so a noisy model doesn't throttle validation cluster.

marco: noted, will add soft-rate-limit param (tokens/sec or checks/sec).

priya: thanks — this feels actionable. if no objections i'll mark the RFC follow-up as "implementable" and open a small PR with the config defs. :thumbsup:

tess: :+1:
